messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — Multiple monitoring probes in eu-west-1 are reporting missing telemetry and intermittent DNS failures. Impact: potential cross-region routing anomalies. Auto-page to on-call. @maria is primary on-call for SRE.

maria: seeing the page. joining. can someone paste the probe IDs? I only have the alert summary right now.

kevin: probe ids: probe-eu-01, probe-eu-03, probe-eu-05. Alerts started ~10:42 UTC. They’re flapping; some probes show 0 packets, others time out. no clear host-level errors yet.

ash: I’m in the network room. I can confirm Route53 healthchecks for those probes returned "no response" briefly. No EC2 instance reboots in that timeframe. Possibly a VPC nat gateway or AZ routing blip.

maria: ok, action plan: 1) triage whether this is monitoring-only (false positives) vs real customer impact. 2) if traffic affected, failover routing to eu-central for affected customers. 3) page net-eng for potential BGP/az fabric issues. @lee can you engage net-eng?

lee: ping @net-eng-bot — please escalate to network-ops. include probe list and timeline.

net-eng-bot: Escalation created: NET-OPS-4872. Assigned to team network-ops-p1. Notifying on-call network engineer.

kevin: quick grep in probe logs shows repeated dns resolution errors to our internal resolver 10.0.0.2 around 10:41:50 - 10:43:10 UTC. Sample log:
```
[10:41:52] resolve cluster-api.prod.redwood -> timeout
[10:42:03] resolve artifacts.s3.eu-west-1 -> SERVFAIL
[10:42:18] no response from 10.0.0.2
```

ash: also saw elevated RTT for our forwarding nat. suspecting control plane update in that AZ hit the route table. Cross-checking control plane events now.

maria: are customer-facing endpoints showing errors? any 5xx spikes in APIGW or proxies?

kevin: quick metrics: 5xx up 0.4% for eu-west-1 for 10:42-10:46 window. A small fraction but noticeable for a few high-throughput customers. No global failover yet.

lee: net-eng reports: "we observed transient route flap in eu-west-1-A, traced to partial route withdrawal from a peering transit gateway during maintenance window, not fully bubbled to regional healthchecks." They’re reverting the change now.

ash: can we suppress alerts for affected probes to avoid noise while net-eng reverts? we should avoid noisy pages if this is in-progress fix.

maria: yes suppress for 15m with a note. I'll annotate the incident and add suppression to monitoring. Also start a canary failover for a low-traffic subset to eu-central to validate routing.

kevin: suppress rule applied to probe-eu-* for 15m: reason "ongoing net-eng remediation". canary failover started for tenant org-42, redirecting API traffic to eu-central.

net-eng-bot: Update from NET-OPS-4872: rollback completed at 10:47:28 UTC. Route propagation stable. Suggest waiting 2 minutes then run probe replay.

ash: running probe replay now (commands):
```
for p in probe-eu-01 probe-eu-03 probe-eu-05; do ./probe-run --id $p --check dns,http; done
```

ash: replay shows probes passing now, DNS resolvers responding, no SERVFAIL. RTT normalized.

kevin: metrics confirm 5xx returned to baseline by 10:49.

maria: status: remediation successful, net-eng rollback fixed the transient route flap. Customer impact: minor, short window (approx 3-5 minutes) of elevated errors for some EU tenants. Action items: 1) net-eng to add guardrail to prevent partial propagation during maintenance 2) SRE to tune probe alert thresholds to avoid false positives on short transient events 3) follow up with monitoring team on missing probe telemetry during the incident (some logs were incomplete).

lee: logged follow-ups: NET-OPS-4873 (guardrail), SRE-234 (probe thresholds), MON-912 (probe telemetry reliability).

maria: handing off to post-incident doc. attaching timeline and query snippets to the ticket. leaving incident channel. @kevin @ash keep an eye for any regression. :thumbsup:

kevin: noted. will watch dashboards for next 30m.

ash: on it. thanks all.

net-eng-bot: Incident NET-OPS-4872 marked resolved. Root cause: partial route withdrawal during maintenance window. Remediation: rollback of change. No further action required for immediate availability.

maria: closing the page. will open postmortem for the customer-impact window and link to NET-OPS-4872 and MON-912. if anyone has anything to add to the timeline, paste here before I archive.
